4432665.headline: Bowers (ankle) will be listed as questionable for Sunday night's game against the Browns, Adam Hill of the Las Vegas Review-Journal reports.
4432665.story: Per Sam Warren of The Athletic, Bowers didn't practice Friday after being limited the previous two days. It's unclear if the star TE's 'DNP' to close the week was maintenance or setback related, but the Raiders' late kickoff presents an issue for those considering Bowers in Week 12 fantasy lineups. As one of the marquee names carrying a 'questionable' tag into the weekend, look for added context regarding his status to arrive no later than Saturday night or Sunday morning via the usual notable NFL insiders.

4432665.headline: Bowers (ankle/quadriceps) wasn't on the field for the portion of Friday's practice open to the media, Ryan McFadden of ESPN.com reports.
4432665.story: Bowers kicked off Week 12 prep with limited listings on the Raiders' first two injury reports, and while he may join his teammates on the practice field at some point Friday, there's now a chance he's a non-participant. He's fighting through ankle and quadriceps injuries that sidelined him this past Sunday at Denver, and Friday's practice report will reveal his activity level and also his odds to suit up Sunday in Cleveland.

4432665.headline: Bowers (ankle) remained a limited participant in Thursday's practice, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.
4432665.story: The star tight end, who was inactive this past Sunday against the Broncos, now has strung together four straight limited practices, which bodes well for his chances of being back for this weekend's game against the Browns. Friday's final injury report will determine whether Bowers carries an injury designation for the contest or is fully cleared for Week 12 action.

4432665.headline: Bowers (ankle) was on the field for Thursday's practice, Ryan McFadden of ESPN.com reports.
4432665.story: Bowers, who was inactive versus Denver in Week 11, logged his third straight limited practice Wednesday, which offers hope that the star TE will be available this weekend against the Browns. Per McFadden, Bowers' right ankle was heavily wrapped up Thursday, which wasn't the case the day before. The Raiders' upcoming injury report will clarify his official participation level in Wednesday' session, in any case.

4685472.headline: McMillan (foot) practiced in a limited capacity Friday, Mike Kaye of ESPN.com reports.
4685472.story: McMillan's return to the practice field generally is a positive sign as he works through a sore foot, but he now has just one more chance to get back to full Saturday, at which point the Panthers may tag him with a designation for Monday's game at Tampa Bay. No matter, head coach Dave Canales has expressed optimism this week that McMillan will be able to go in Week 12, per Kaye.

4685472.headline: McMillan (foot) was not in uniform for the team stretch portion of Friday's practice, but he did suit up afterward, Joe Person of The Athletic reports.
4685472.story: Mike Kaye of ESPN.com reported earlier Friday that McMillan was in a helmet and pads, and although he ditched them while stretching he put them back on shortly afterward. Ultimately, Friday's injury report will include McMillan's activity level, if any, after he was listed as a non-participant on Thursday's practice estimate due to a sore foot.

4685472.headline: McMillan (foot) was wearing a helmet and pads ahead of Friday's practice, Mike Kaye of ESPN.com reports.
4685472.story: McMillan was listed as a DNP on Thursday's estimated injury report due to a sore foot, but his return one day later backs up head coach Dave Canales' expressed optimism to Kaye about the wide receiver's status for Week 12. Friday's practice report will reveal McMillan's activity level.

4685472.headline: McMillan (foot) was listed as a DNP on Thursday's practice estimate, Mike Kaye of ESPN.com reports.
4685472.story: After McMillan didn't participate in Wednesday's unofficial practice due to a sore foot, head coach Dave Canales told Kaye that the team is "optimistic" that the wide receiver will play Monday at Tampa Bay. McMillan will have two more chances to mix into drills this week before the Panthers potentially tag him with a designation for Week 12 action.

4429615.headline: Flowers (ankle) was listed as a full participant in Thursday's practice.
4429615.story: Flowers was limited at practice Wednesday, but the wide receiver's quick return to all activity one day later clears the way for him to suit up Sunday against the Texans. In his last outing, Flowers (who has recorded a fantasy-friendly 57-785-3 line on 82 targets through 10 games), was on the field for 88 percent of his team's snaps on offense in a 35-33 loss to the Panthers in Week 11 en route to catching eight of his game-high 11 targets for 97 yards.

4429615.headline: Flowers (ankle) was listed as a limited participant in Wednesday's practice.
4429615.story: The same applies to fellow starting WR Rashod Bateman (groin), with the duo's status now worth tracking an advance of Sunday's game against the Texans. 4429615.headline: Flowers caught eight of 11 targets for 97 yards in Sunday's 35-33 loss to the Panthers.
4429615.story: No other Raven caught more than four passes or saw more than six targets as Flowers continues to build chemistry with new quarterback Jacoby Brissett. The fourth-year wideout has posted a 14-171-0 line on 18 targets in Brissett's first two starts for Baltimore, immediately establishing a strong floor. Flowers will try to keep rolling in Week 12 against what has been a surprisingly vulnerable Texans defense.

4241416.headline: Hubbard carried the ball 27 times for 120 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 35-33 win over the Ravens. He added a two-point conversion.
4241416.story: The 27-year-old running back continues to shine, making two trips to the end zone for a second straight week and piling up at least 120 rushing yards for the third time in 2026. Hubbard is handling a bell-cow workload with no issues, and over six games since the Panthers' bye he's averaging nearly 25 touches a game while amassing 688 scrimmage yards and six rushing touchdowns. 4432620.headline: Washington (shoulder) will be out for Sunday's game against the Titans and is considered week-to-week moving forward, Demetrius Harvey of the Florida Times-Union reports.
4432620.story: Washington was added to Jacksonville's injury report Thursday due to a shoulder injury, and the impact of the injury has escalated from limiting his practice participation Thursday to sidelining Jacksonville's top receiver Sunday and possibly beyond then. In Washington's absence, Jakobi Meyers (ankle), Brian Thomas, Josh Cameron and possibly Travis Hunter or CJ Williams -- to a lesser degree -- could garner more attention from Trevor Lawrence against a Titans secondary that has allowed the most catches and yards per game in the league to wide receivers. 4432620.headline: Washington (shoulder) was listed as a limited participant in Thursday's practice, Ryan O'Halloran of The Florida Times-Union reports.
4432620.story: Washington wasn't on Wednesday's injury report, so his addition to it a day later is certainly of note. It remains to be seen if the WR, who is coming off consecutive big games for the Jaguars, is managing a shoulder issue stemming from Week 11 action or was hurt in Thursday's practice. Friday's report will reveal both Washington's participation level to close the week, as well as his game status for a 1:00 p.m. ET matchup versus the Titans on Sunday.

4432620.headline: Washington secured eight of 17 targets for 103 yards in the Jaguars' 23-18 loss to the Giants on Sunday.
4432620.story: Washington led the Jaguars across the board in receptions, receiving yards and targets, and his day could have been even better had what appeared to be an acrobatic touchdown catch in the back of the end zone early in the fourth quarter not been ruled incomplete. Washington still made several tough grabs throughout the afternoon against a stingy Giants secondary, and he now has consecutive 100-yard efforts for the first time in 2026. Washington needs just 100 receiving yards to eclipse his career high of 847 heading into a very favorable Week 12 home matchup against the Titans next Sunday.

4870653.headline: Concepcion caught three of eight targets for 21 yards in Sunday's 27-24 win over Houston. He also gained six yards on one carry.
4870653.story: Concepcion finished second on the Browns in targets behind tight end Harold Fannin, who had nine. However, whereas Fannin was able to turn his looks into seven receptions and 91 yards, Concepcion posted a much more modest 3-21-0 line. The rookie wideout departed to the medical tent during the first half of the game due to an undisclosed issue, but he was able to quickly return. Concepcion hasn't put up prolific numbers this season, but he does have at least three receptions in eight of his 10 appearances. 4870653.headline: Concepcion (undisclosed) returned to Sunday's game against the Texans, Scott Petrak of the Elyria Chronicle-Telegram reports.
4870653.story: Concepcion visited the medical tent in the first half of this Week 10 matchup, but his absence didn't last long. He'll continue to operate as one of the Browns' top two wide receivers along with Denzel Boston.

4870653.headline: Concepcion (undisclosed) headed to the medical tent during Sunday's game against the Texans, Scott Petrak of the Elyria Chronicle-Telegram reports.
4870653.story: Per Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN, prior to that Concepcion was slow to get up after dropping a deep pass from QB Deshaun Watson. The rookie WR has one catch for six yards (on four targets) to his credit thus far in Sunday's contest.

4036378.story: Love already had a daunting challenge coming in against a talented Rams secondary. It was made exponentially more difficult due to Christian Watson, to whom he threw his only touchdown pass of the night in the second quarter from six yards out, exiting the game for good late in the first half due to a possible concussion. The veteran signal-caller unsurprisingly scuffled throughout, and his two interceptions came in the second half while the game was still within reach for Green Bay. 4036378.headline: Love completed 17 of 27 passes for 220 yards and a touchdown with an interception in Sunday's 30-10 loss to the Vikings.
4036378.story: The 28-year-old QB came into the game having been sacked just 17 times in his first nine games of the season, but Minnesota brought Love down eight times Sunday. Despite that onslaught, he was able to find J. Michael Sturdivant for a 32-yard TD in the third quarter to salvage his line slightly. It was the first time since Week 6 that Love had failed to throw multiple touchdowns, and just the second time all season. He'll get a Week 11 bye to heal up from Sunday's pummeling before facing Myles Garrett and the Rams in Week 12.

4685247.headline: Allen rushed 16 times for 75 yards while catching his lone target for nine yards in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Chargers.
4685247.story: Allen's 16 carries matched his total from the previous two games combined, as he had seen a downtick in opportunities since fellow RB Breece Hall returned from a quadriceps injury. Hall led the backfield once again with 100 scrimmage yards and a touchdown on 23 touches, but Allen was a key part of the game plan as well in the run-heavy win. The Jets will face a one-win team for a second consecutive game in Week 12 at Miami, which could allow Allen to stay involved alongside Hall.

4685247.headline: Allen rushed eight times for 40 yards and caught his only target for six yards in Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Bills.
4685247.story: For a second consecutive game, Allen was outplayed by Breece Hall, who produced 108 scrimmage yards on 15 touches. Allen remains the more efficient runner, averaging 5.0 yards per carry to Hall's 3.4 this season, but Hall is the team's preferred option in passing situations, which have been plentiful with the 2-8 Jets frequently in catch-up mode. Perhaps a Week 11 matchup with a Chargers team that's still searching for its first win through Sunday of Week 10 will offer an opportunity to stick with the run and play to Allen's strengths.

4360569.headline: Mason rushed 11 times for 38 yards while catching his lone target for minus-1 yard in Sunday's 35-10 loss to the 49ers.
4360569.story: Mason had one more carry and eight more rushing yards than Aaron Jones, but Jones' totals included an 11-yard touchdown run in the first quarter. They have worked in a near-even split when both veteran RBs have been healthy, but Mason hasn't scored since Week 1. Between his lack of TDs and minimal involvement as a pass catcher (three receptions for six yards in six games), Mason hasn't provided much fantasy value ahead of a Week 12 home game against the Falcons.

4360569.headline: Mason carried the ball 16 times for 59 yards and failed to catch his only target in Sunday's 30-10 win over the Packers.
4360569.story: The fifth-year RB led the Vikings in rushing yards, but Aaron Jones was the more productive player in the backfield, gaining 55 scrimmage yards on 12 touches and scoring on a one-yard plunge in the second quarter. Mason has yet to get into the end zone in four games since returning from a thumb injury, piecing together 182 rushing yards on 4.0 yards per carry while working in a timeshare with Jones. He could break that drought in Week 11 in a potential revenge game against the 49ers.

4360569.story: Mason was markedly more efficient than backfield mate Aaron Jones with his opportunities, averaging 5.8 yards per carry compared to the latter's 3.2. Both backs' touches were limited due to game script, however, but Mason's YPC was an encouraging figure. The veteran back next takes aim at the Packers defense in a Week 10 road matchup on Sunday.

4689936.headline: Bates made both of his field-goal attempts and three of his four extra-point tries during Detroit's 39-35 loss to the Bears on Thursday.
4689936.story: Bates' missed extra point came from 48 yards out due to a 15-yard taunting penalty. The 27-year-old has now converted 19 of his 21 field-goal attempts and 36 of his 37 extra-point tries across 11 games this season.

4689936.headline: Bates made one of two field-goal attempts and all four PATs in Sunday's 31-21 win over the Bucs.
4689936.story: The kicker missed a 53-yard try on the Lions' opening drive of the game but later came back to make one from 56 yards in the second quarter. Through 10 games this season, Bates is 17-for-19 on field-goal attempts and a perfect 33-for-33 on extra points. Bates led the league in PATs in the 2024 and 2025 seasons and is again on pace to kick 50-plus extra points in 2026.

4689936.headline: Bates made all five of his PATs in the Lions' 35-10 win over the Patriots on Sunday in Munich.
4689936.story: Bates did not attempt a field goal in the contest. He remains 16-for-17 on field-goal attempts and moves to 29-for-29 on PATs through nine regular-season games in 2026.

4689936.headline: Bates went 4-for-4 on field-goal attempts and made his only extra-point try during Sunday's 19-9 win over the Dolphins.
4689936.story: Bates was able to make multiple field goals for the third straight game after having done so just once over the team's first five contests this year. The kicker converted attempts from 28 and 40 yards in the first half before adding makes from 33 and 43 yards after the break. Bates has now gone 16-for-17 on field-goal tries while making all 24 of his PATs over eight games during the 2026 campaign to this point.

4426338.headline: Nix completed 22 of 40 passes for 169 yards, no touchdowns and two interceptions in Friday's 27-5 loss to the Steelers. He also rushed once for seven yards and lost a fumble.
4426338.story: Nix was directly responsible for two first-half Pittsburgh touchdowns, as T.J. Watt recovered a Nix fumble in the end zone to open the scoring and Jalen Ramsey scored on a pick-six to extend Pittsburgh's lead to 24-5. Neither offense did much after halftime as Nix continued to struggle. Friday's dud drops Nix's season average to just 193 passing yards per game to go with a 12:7 TD:INT through 11 starts, but the Broncos still boast an excellent 8-3 record heading into a Week 13 home game against the Dolphins.

4426338.story: After a hit-or-miss first six appearances of the season, Nix has settled into a four-game stretch in which his passing yards have ranged from 222 to 237 weekly, a span in which he boasts a 6:2 TD:INT and 84 rushing yards and another score. He also displayed some promise with offseason acquisition Jaylen Waddle (3-61-0 on six targets) while connecting with TE Adam Trautman for his 12th touchdown pass in 10 contests. Nix will look to keep things rolling Friday at Pittsburgh.

2576925.headline: Waller (knee) practiced in a limited fashion Friday.
2576925.story: Waller was among four Panthers tight ends to have a capped session Friday, the others being Tommy Tremble (knee), Mitchell Evans (Achilles) and Feleipe Franks (wrist). Waller was able to play through his knee injury this past Sunday against the Ravens, when he handled a 46 percent snap share en route to three catches (on three targets) for 42 yards.

2576925.headline: Waller (knee) was listed as limited on Thursday's estimated injury report, Mike Kaye of ESPN.com reports.
2576925.story: For s second week in a row, Waller is dealing with a knee injury, but his listing to begin this week implies he's a bit healthier after kicking off Week 11 prep with a DNP. He'll have two more opportunities to practice in full Friday and Saturday before the Panthers potentially make a call on his status for Monday's game at Tampa Bay.

2576925.headline: Waller caught all three of his targets for 42 yards in Sunday's 35-33 win over the Ravens.
2576925.story: The veteran tight end was out-produced by second-year player Mitchell Evans, who posted a 5-44-1 line on five targets, but Waller made more of an impact than Tommy Tremble, who caught his only target for 18 yards. With all three members of the trio capable of making a splash in any given week, Waller will be tough to rely on heading into a Week 12 meeting with the Buccaneers.

2576925.headline: Waller (knee) is listed as active Sunday against the Ravens, Darin Gantt of the Panthers' official site reports.
2576925.story: The Panthers kicked off Week 11 prep with their top two tight ends (Waller and Tommy Tremble) not practicing due to knee injuries, after which head coach Dave Canales told Steve Reed of the Associated Press that those issues were a "concern." Both Waller and Tremble were limited Thursday and Friday and entered the weekend listed as questionable. Now that Waller is confirmed to be active -- along with Tremble -- the former will look to continue to build upon his 25-323-4 line on 39 targets that he's accrued in nine appearances this season.

4429795.headline: Gibbs carried the ball 21 times for 205 yards and three touchdowns while catching all five of his targets for 47 yards in Thursday's 39-35 loss to the Bears.
4429795.story: The superstar running back was already headed for a career-best season coming into Week 12, but Gibbs took things to another level on Thanksgiving, producing his third career game with three rushing scores and his second with 200-plus rushing yards. The 252 scrimmage yards also tied his season high, a mark he reached just two weeks ago against the Patriots. Gibbs leads the NFL with 1,754 scrimmage yards, and given his current form he could reach 2,000 as soon as next week, on the road against the Falcons.

4567048.headline: The Chiefs ruled out Walker (groin) for Thursday's game against the Bills.
4567048.story: Though Walker was able to log a limited practice Tuesday, he was listed as a non-participant Wednesday and will wind up missing a third straight contest while he continues to nurse a sore groin. With Walker sidelined, rookie Emmett Johnson is set for another turn as the Chiefs' lead back, with Jaydn Ott serving as his top backup and Nate Carter a possible practice-squad elevation. Given that the Chiefs on are on a short week, Walker -- who last saw game action Nov. 8 -- will have added time to heal before the team's next contest Dec. 3 against the Rams.

4567048.headline: The Chiefs listed Walker (groin) as a limited participant in Tuesday's practice.
4567048.story: After he had been listed as a non-participant on five straight injury reports and missed two games along the way, Walker was able to take a step forward Tuesday as he works his way back from a sore groin. Per Nate Taylor of ESPN.com, head coach Andy Reid said prior to the session that Walker was "feeling pretty good," while noting that Tuesday's practice would be important in deciding whether the running back suits up Thursday versus the Bills. Though Walker will reclaim a starting role if he ultimately gets cleared to play Thanksgiving Day, he could wind up ceding more snaps and touches to ro

4567048.headline: Chiefs head coach Andy Reid said that Walker (groin) will practice Tuesday, Nate Taylor of ESPN.com reports. "I'm not anticipating a ton of work," Reid said. "Let's see how does. He's feeling pretty good."
4567048.story: Walker has been sidelined for the Chiefs' last two games due to a sore groin and was listed as a non-participant in Monday's practice. Though the running back appears poised to take a step forward in terms of activity Tuesday, Reid's comments suggest that Walker will likely be a limited participant. The Chiefs will wait and see how Walker responds to practice Tuesday before having a better feel for his status for Thursday's game against the Bills.

4567048.headline: Walker (groin) was listed as a non-participant on Monday's practice estimate.
4567048.story: Since the Chiefs are coming off a 34-7 win over the Cardinals on Sunday, the team held a walkthrough Monday in preparation for Thursday's game against the Bills. Nate Taylor of ESPN.com previously reported that the Chiefs are "optimistic" that Walker may be available for the team's Thanksgiving night contest, but with one 'DNP' now on the books, the running back has two more opportunities to log any listed level of practice participation before the team posts its Week 12 game statuses.

4361370.headline: Olave caught nine of 15 targets for 102 yards in Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Bears.
4361370.story: One week after taking a back seat to rookie Jordyn Tyson, Olave re-emerged as Tyler Shough's favorite downfield option, as he set a new season high in targets and topped 100 receiving yards for the fourth time in 2026. Tyson, meanwhile, caught only one pass on two targets, suggesting the Saints' aerial attack may not be able to support both wideouts in the same game. Olave will look to make an impact again in Week 12 against the Bengals.

3040151.headline: Kittle caught all three of his targets for 34 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 35-10 win over the Vikings.
3040151.story: Kittle scored on both of his first-half catches, capping San Francisco's opening drive with a 17-yard touchdown before adding an eight-yard score in the first minute of the second quarter. The multi-touchdown performance was especially impressive considering the Vikings came in having allowed just one touchdown on a league-low 33 catches to tight ends. Kittle has been one of the top performers at his position as usual, with seven touchdown catches in 10 games, though his streak of consecutive outings with at least four catches ended at eight games. 3040151.story: Kittle put together a very solid fantasy performance that was easily lost in the shuffle of multiple spectacular efforts by players on either side. However, the veteran tight end did pace the 49ers in receptions and targets while finishing second in receiving yards, and he's now recorded at least 70 yards on five occasions this season. Kittle is up to a 44-557-5 line on 62 targets through nine games as a Week 11 home showdown against the Vikings next Sunday night approaches.

3040151.headline: Kittle caught four of seven targets for 58 yards in Sunday's 38-17 win over the Raiders.
3040151.story: Kittle had at least three more targets than any teammate Sunday but finished 28 receiving yards shy of Jordan Watkins' team-leading total, while Brock Purdy's two touchdown passes went to Christian McCaffrey and Watkins. Sunday's output marked Kittle's third-lowest yardage total of the season, but the star TE recorded at least four catches for a seventh consecutive game. He'll look to add to his season totals of 38 catches for 483 yards and five touchdowns in Week 10 against the Cowboys.

4361741.headline: Head coach Kyle Shanahan said Friday that Purdy (ankle) has been ruled out for Sunday's game versus the Seahawks, Jennifer Lee Chan of NBC Sports Bay Area reports.
4361741.story: Purdy wasn't able to practice during Week 12 prep due to an ankle injury, which will sideline him for the first time this season. In place of Purdy, Mac Jones will earn the spot start Sunday, while the former's next chance to suit up is Sunday, Nov. 6, at the Giants. Shanahan added that surgery isn't on the table for Purdy and he's optimistic the QB will be OK to return in Week 13, according to Nick Wagoner of ESPN.com.

4361741.headline: Purdy (ankle) wasn't spotted during the portion of Friday's practice open to the media, Matt Barrows of The Athletic reports.
4361741.story: Purdy appears poised to be listed as a non-participant for a third consecutive day during Week 12 prep as he tends to an ankle injury. Head coach Kyle Shanahan has yet to speak on Purdy's health concern, but Friday's practice report will reveal if the quarterback is in danger of missing Sunday's game against the Seahawks.

4361741.headline: Purdy (ankle) was listed as a non-participant on Thursday's injury report, Eric Branch of the San Francisco Chronicle reports.
4361741.story: Purdy has kicked off Week 12 prep with back-to-back DNPs due to an ankle injury, giving him just one more chance to mix into drills Friday before the 49ers potentially tag him with a designation for Sunday's showdown with the Seahawks. There's been no indication that Purdy is in danger of missing that contest, but if it comes to pass, Mac Jones is available to start under center.

4361741.headline: Purdy didn't practice Wednesday due to an ankle injury, Vic Tafur of The Athletic reports.
4361741.story: Purdy put on a master class during this past Sunday's 35-10 win against the Vikings in Mexico City, completing 21 of 26 passes for 255 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions. Now with a health concern in tow, his status will be monitored closely to get a sense of his odds to suit up Sunday against the Seahawks. Mac Jones is waiting in the wings in the event Purdy isn't able to play in Week 12.

3042519.headline: Jones rushed eight times for 30 yards and a touchdown while catching his lone target for 13 yards in Sunday's 35-10 loss to the 49ers.
3042519.story: Jones tied the game with an 11-yard rushing touchdown in the first quarter, but the 49ers outscored the Vikings 21-3 in the second quarter, forcing Minnesota into a more pass-heavy approach. Jordan Mason led the team with 38 rushing yards on 11 carries. Jones and Mason should continue to split carries in Week 12 against the Falcons, with Jones offering greater upside as a pass catcher.

3042519.headline: Jones carried the ball 11 times for 47 yards and a touchdown and caught his only target for eight yards in Sunday's 30-10 win over the Packers.
3042519.story: Jordan Mason led the Vikings with 59 rushing yards, but Jones had the more productive afternoon as he scored his first TD since Week 5 on a one-yard plunge in the second quarter. Jones' upside will remain limited while working in a timeshare with Mason, but he's still got some utility heading into a Week 11 clash with the 49ers.

3042519.story: Jones and backfield mate Jordan Mason combined for just 11 carries on an abysmal night for the Vikings offense, and the latter was much more efficient than Jones by averaging 5.8 yards per carry on his six totes. Jones now has seen his rushing yardage totals drop in three straight games, and Mason's return from injured reserve has played a role in the former seeing just 18 total carries in the last three contests. Jones retains a very modest outlook for a Week 10 road matchup against his old Packers teammates Sunday.

4701936.story: Golden saw Christian Watson exit for good late in the first half due to a possible concussion, but the former still couldn't capitalize on a night when Jordan Love threw for a modest 198 yards and tossed two interceptions. Golden's yardage total tied for his second-lowest figure of the season, while Wednesday marked his first game without multiple receptions. Golden will look to bounce back in a Week 13 road matchup against the Saints on Sunday, Dec. 6.

The kicker made a 56-yarder in the first quarter before later adding makes from 31 and 41 yards in the fourth quarter. 2971573.headline: Fairbairn went 2-for-2 on field-goal attempts and converted his only PAT in Sunday's 27-21 overtime loss to the Giants.
2971573.story: Fairbairn finished off each of the Texans' first two scoring drives with field-goal makes from 58 and 57 yards in the first half. The kicker has now converted multiple field goals in four straight contests, and his last miss came all the way back in Week 2 versus Cincinnati. Fairbairn has gone 15-for-16 on field-goal tries, including 6-for-7 from 50-plus yards, while making all 16 of his extra-point attempts over seven contests so far.

4433970.story: McCarthy continued to look like a competent NFL signal-caller in his third start for the Giants, posting a new career high in passing yards and adding a new season high in rushing yardage. His one touchdown pass was a critical one, as he hit Isaiah Likely over the middle for a 66-yard score just before the midway point of the fourth quarter to erase a 17-14 deficit. McCarthy has displayed excellent chemistry with his top targets, and he'll look to keep his hot streak going against a pass-funnel Jaguars defense in a Week 11 home matchup on Sunday, Nov. 22.

4433970.headline: McCarthy (hip pointer) is "good to go" and isn't expected to be limited for Thursday's game against the Commanders, James Palmer of NFL Network reports.
4433970.story: McCarthy missed much of the third quarter of this past Sunday's win at Philadelphia due to a hip pointer but was able to return to action, completing 12 of 19 passes for 127 yards, no touchdowns and no interceptions and rushing four times for 22 yards. Considering he ended Week 10 prep with back-to-back full practices, he seemingly was in the clear for Thursday's matchup, and Palmer's report indicates McCarthy will take on every rep, leaving Jameis Winston as the No. 2 QB, and on the sidelines Thursday.

4432773.story: Thomas has had a disappointing third season in Jacksonville, mustering a meager 84 receiving yards over his last eight appearances while seemingly having fallen out of favor in coach Liam Coen's offense. Washington's absence against Tennessee's struggling secondary could provide Thomas with an opportunity to turn back the clock and put up a performance reminiscent of the 2024 first-round pick's elite rookie season. Jakobi Meyers and Josh Cameron also are in line for expanded roles in Jacksonville's wide-receiver room.

4432773.headline: Thomas caught one pass for an 18-yard touchdown on three targets in Sunday's 23-18 loss to the Giants.
4432773.story: Thomas' three targets were a distant fourth on the team, as Parker Washington (17), Jakobi Meyers (10) and Josh Cameron (seven) combined to see a combined 34 looks on Trevor Lawrence's 47 pass attempts. Thomas ran 32 routes, 14 more than Cameron as the Jaguars' nominal WR3, but the former hasn't been seeing meaningful target volume for months. After drawing nine targets in Week 2, Thomas has averaged 2.1 targets per game over his last eight contests. He's well off the fantasy radar while Washington and Meyers are healthy.

4432773.headline: Thomas caught three of four targets for 29 yards in Sunday's 40-23 win over the Titans.
4432773.story: The three catches tied his season high, while the four targets represented his biggest volume since Week 2. The Jaguars' decision not to deal Thomas at the trade deadline remains a curious one, as the third-year wideout simply doesn't have a significant role in Liam Coen's offense and might not step into one even if someone like Parker Washington got injured -- Josh Cameron was more productive Sunday on three targets and caught one of Trevor Lawrence's three TDs. Thomas will take a 13-146-2 line on 26 targets over nine games into a Week 11 tilt against the Giants.

4432773.headline: The Jaguars have relayed to inquiring teams that they intend to keep Thomas through Tuesday's trade deadline, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reports.
4432773.story: After sending out a first-round pick, two second-round picks, a fifth-round pick and a sixth-round pick Monday in separate deals to bring in defenders Jordan Davis, Jessie Bates and Davon Godchaux, the Jaguars likely could have recouped some of that draft capital if they had opted to move Thomas. Instead, Fowler indicates that the Jaguars plan to keep the rest of their roster intact ahead of the deadline, which will result in Thomas sticking around. 4426515.story: Nacua is also dealing with a PCL sprain and turf toe, but the only procedure he required was for his MCL. With a firmer 4-to-5-month timeline now in place for the star wideout, he'll be done for the season while the Rams look to others to help fill the massive void in their receiver corps. 4426515.headline: Coach Sean McVay revealed Friday that Nacua (knee) had surgery to repair his MCL on Tuesday and is on track to miss a couple of months, Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports.
4426515.story: Given that timetable, Nacua -- who already is on injured reserve -- could be out for the rest of the regular season, which is a huge blow to the Rams' pass-catching corps going forward. In Nacua's continued absence, Konata Mumpfield, CJ Daniels, Tutu Atwell and Xavier Smith are the team's healthy options at WR, though fellow starter Davante Adams (hamstring) is believed to be targeting a return in Week 12 following the team's bye.

4426515.headline: Nacua has been suspended three games for violating the NFL's personal conduct policy, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
4426515.story: Nacua currently resides on injured reserve due to PCL and MCL sprains and a turf toe injury, for which he still must miss at least three games. 3916387.story: Last Friday, head coach Jesse Minter announced that Jackson was facing a projected recovery timeline of 6-to-10 weeks after requiring a procedure to address a broken and dislocated thumb. Given that the Patriots are already close to the limit of how many players they can designate for return from injured reserve, Maye isn't a lock to land on IR, but he's nonetheless facing an absence longer than the required four games that a placement on IR would mandate. For now, Tommy DeVito has been installed as the team's starter ahead of its Week 12 matchup against the Chargers, with rookie Behren Morton on hand as his backup.

A return at some point down the stretch likely will depend on the Patriots remaining in the playoff race, but for the time being Tommy DeVito will be under center in place of Maye.

Shakir will look to build on this outing as he searches for his second TD of the season Thursday against the Chiefs.

3128429.headline: Sutton caught one of eight targets for four yards in Friday's 27-5 loss to the Steelers.
3128429.story: Denver's entire offense struggled mightily, generating just three points while allowing Pittsburgh's defense to score two touchdowns off turnovers by Bo Nix. Sutton was right down there with Nix among Friday's worst performers in an outing reminiscent of Week 4 at San Francisco, when Sutton caught one of six targets for four yards. The 31-year-old WR has caught just one of 10 targets over the past two games, and Sutton has secured less than half of his targets (26 of 56) heading into a Week 13 home game against the Dolphins.

3128429.headline: Sutton didn't corral either of his two targets during Sunday's 38-24 victory versus the Raiders.
3128429.story: Sutton thus was blanked in the box score for the first time Week 7 of the 2024 campaign, a span of 39 games (including playoffs). Considering he's surpassed 50 receiving yards just one time in 10 appearances in 2026, he doesn't hold much sway for fantasy purposes, especially in a Broncos offense that often has sputtered this season. Sutton's next chance to turn the tide arrives Friday at Pittsburgh.

3128429.headline: Sutton caught five of nine targets for 45 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 26-21 win over the Panthers.
3128429.story: The five grabs and nine targets led the Broncos on the day, but Pat Bryant just edged him out for the receiving yards lead. The highlight of Sutton's solid performance was a three-yard TD from Bo Nix in the first quarter, as none of his receptions went for longer than 12 yards. Denver gets a well-timed bye in Week 10, but if Jaylen Waddle (concussion) isn't cleared to play on the other side of it, Sutton could see bigger volume in Week 11 against the Raiders. On the season, the long-time Bronco sports a 25-266-2 line on 46 targets through nine games.

3128429.headline: Sutton caught all four of his targets for 53 yards in Sunday's 28-24 win over Kansas City.
3128429.story: For the fourth straight game, Sutton failed to see more than five targets, but his four grabs and 53 yards were both season highs. It's been a rough campaign so far for the 31-year-old receiver in an inconsistent Broncos aerial attack, and Sutton will take a 20-221-1 line on 37 targets through eight games intro a Week 9 clash with the Panthers.

4429205.headline: Addison (thumb) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Falcons, Dane Mizutani of the St. Paul Pioneer Press reports.
4429205.story: Addison thus will miss a third straight contest due to a thumb injury that required surgery. In Addison's continued absence, the Vikings will lean on Justin Jefferson, Jauan Jennings, Tai Felton, Myles Price and Jeshaun Jones at wide receiver. Addison's next chance for game action is Sunday, Dec. 6, versus the Panthers.

4429205.headline: Addison (thumb) was listed as a non-participant on Thursday's injury report.
4429205.story: Addison's next listing on an injury report that isn't a DNP will be his first since Nov. 13, when he suffered a thumb injury that required surgery and so far has sidelined him for two games. Head coach Kevin O'Connell relayed to Ben Goessling of The Minnesota Star Tribune on Monday that Addison is "progressing well" in his recovery but is unlikely to play Sunday against the Falcons. Ultimately, Addison's status for Week 12 may be clarified once the Vikings post Friday's practice report.

4429205.headline: Head coach Kevin O'Connell said Addison will be listed as a non-participant on Wednesday's injury report, Ben Goessling of the Minnesota Star Tribune reports.
4429205.story: Addison is in recovery mode from the thumb injury that required surgery following a Nov. 15 practice, and he's missed the last two games as a result. While an IR stint has been ruled out for Addison, O'Connell relayed Monday that the wide receiver is "progressing really well" but also isn't expected to play Sunday against the Falcons, according to Goessling. As long as Addison is sidelined, some combination of Jauan Jennings, Tai Felton and Myles Price will operate alongside top WR Justin Jefferson.

4429205.headline: Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell said Monday that Addison is "progressing really well" in his recovery from thumb surgery, though the wide receiver isn't expected to be available in Week 12 versus the Falcons, Ben Goessling of The Minnesota Star Tribune reports.
4429205.story: Addison injured his thumb during a Week 10 practice and was sidelined for the Vikings' Nov. 15 win over the Packers before undergoing surgery this past week. He remained out for Sunday's 35-10 loss to the 49ers and looks headed for a third straight absence this weekend, but Addison avoided placement on injured reserve and could have a realistic chance at returning to action in Week 13. Jauan Jennings and Tai Felton are likely to be the main beneficiaries from playing-time standpoints while Addison is unavailable.

4362081.headline: Dicker made his lone field-goal attempt and all three PATs in Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Jets.
4362081.story: Dicker's field goal was drilled from 52 yards, and he's now 19-for-21 on field-goal tries and 15-for-15 on extra points through 10 games this season. In a Chargers offense struggling mightily to score points, Dicker's fantasy value has tanked this season.

4362081.headline: Dicker made all three of his field-goal tries and converted both of his extra-point attempts during Monday's 23-20 win at Baltimore.
4362081.story: Dicker's longest field goal on the day was only from 38 yards out, but his accuracy played a big part in the Chargers picking up their first win of the season. He hasn't missed a kick since Week 3, but the team's general inability to move the ball consistently keeps him from projecting as a top-tier fantasy option in most formats going into a Week 11 matchup versus the Jets.

4362081.headline: Dicker went 3-for-3 on field-goal attempts and made his only PAT during Sunday's 44-22 loss to Houston.
4362081.story: Dicker was able to make multiple field-goal tries for the third straight game and fifth time this season. The kicker did all his damage in the first half, converting field goals from 52, 33 and 43 yards before the break. Dicker has now gone 15-for-17 on field-goal attempts, including 1-for-2 from 50-plus yards, over eight contests so far during the 2026 campaign.

4362081.headline: Dicker made all three of his field-goal attempts during Sunday's 24-9 loss against the Rams. He did not kick any extra-point tries.
4362081.story: The Chargers offense put forth another poor effort in Week 8, with four of their 11 drives ending in punts and another three ending with turnovers. Dicker has mostly been efficient through his first seven games of the season, making 12 of his 14 field-goal attempts, but until the offense demonstrates it can consistently move the ball down the field, he'll be hard to trust as a fantasy option.

4697815.headline: White turned two kickoff returns into 48 yards during Monday's 22-20 win over the Bengals.
4697815.story: With Jacory Croskey-Merritt back from a four-game absence due to a groin injury, White saw a season-low 15 snaps on offense, and the latter's lone carry early in the fourth quarter was nullified by a defensive offside penalty. Croskey-Merritt and Austin Ekeler were responsible for 20 of the Commanders' 26 rushing attempts Monday, and it looks like the return of the former has squeezed White out of the offensive gameplan. The Commanders will hit the road for each of their next two games, starting with Sunday against the Cardinals.

4697815.headline: White (heel) is active for Monday's game against the Bengals.
4697815.story: White showed up on the Commanders' Week 11 injury report Friday as limited due to a heel issue and then didn't practice Saturday, leaving him questionable to play Monday. While he's confirmed to be available, he also will be welcoming back Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) from IR for the first time since Week 5, which may eat into White's workload.

4697815.headline: White (heel) is listed as questionable for Monday's game versus the Bengals.
4697815.story: White was added to the Commanders' Week 11 injury report Friday as limited due to a heel issue, and he followed it up with a DNP one day later before getting tagged ahead of Monday's matchup. At the same time, current IR member Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) completed a full week of drills and also is listed as questionable. If he's activated by Monday afternoon, he'll vie with Austin Ekeler and White for touches, assuming the latter avoids inactive status about 90 minutes before an 8:15 p.m. ET kickoff.

4697815.headline: White (heel) is trending toward being available for Monday's game against the Bengals, Tashan Reed of The Washington Post reports.
4697815.story: White has been working through a heel injury, but head coach Dan Quinn told reporters Saturday that the fifth-year running back should be available to play. White has operated as the Commanders' RB1 over the team's last four games, but his role will likely shrink for Week 11 given that Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) is expected to be activated off injured reserve ahead of Monday night's game.

2473037.headline: Myers missed his sole field-goal attempt and made three PATs in the Seahawks' 21-13 win over the Raiders on Sunday.
2473037.story: Myers missed a 44-yard field-goal attempt with 7:05 remaining in the game that would have put the Seahawks up 14 points. The kicker is now 16-for-19 on field-goal attempts and 21-for-23 on PATs over 10 regular-season contests in 2026.

2473037.headline: Myers made his only field-goal attempt and converted both of his extra-point tries during Sunday's 17-3 win versus the Cardinals.
2473037.story: The Seahawks' offense put forth a relatively modest showing in Week 9 with backup quarterback Drew Lock (oblique) at the helm, but Myers made good on the few opportunities that he did have, rebounding somewhat from a rough game in Week 8 where he missed two kicks. Starting quarterback Sam Darnold (quadriceps) will again be out in Week 10 at Las Vegas, but Myers will at least have the benefit of kicking indoors come Sunday.

2473037.headline: Myers missed his lone field-goal attempt and made one of two PATs in Monday night's 34-17 loss to the Bears.
2473037.story: Myers converted a chip-shot 27-yard field goal in the second quarter but later missed an extra point wide to the left before halftime. He then had a 33-yard field-goal try blocked in the fourth quarter. On the season, the veteran kicker is 14-for-16 on FGAs and 17-for-19 on PATs. He'll be a kicker to stream next Sunday at home against the Cardinals.

2473037.headline: Myers went 2-for-2 on field-goal tries and made both of his PATs during Sunday night's 20-3 win over the Chiefs.
2473037.story: Myers was able to make multiple field goals for the third straight game, converting a 25-yarder in the second quarter before later adding a 35-yard make in the second half. The kicker has now gone 14-for-15 on field-goal tries, including 3-for-3 from 50-plus yards, over the first seven games of the 2026 campaign.

3055899.headline: Butker made one of two field-goal attempts and his lone PAT in Thursday night's 13-10 loss to the Bills.
3055899.story: After making a 26-yard field goal earlier in the game, Butker missed wide right from 46 yards in the fourth quarter, leaving the score tied 10-10 following an 11-play drive. It was Butker's eighth missed field goal of the season, and he's also missed an extra point. Butker has converted a career-low 65.2 percent of his field-goal tries in 2026. The Chiefs may need to make a move at the position ahead of next Thursday's date with the Rams.

3055899.headline: Butker made both of his field-goal attempts while going 4-for-4 on extra-point tries during Sunday's 34-7 win over the Cardinals.
3055899.story: Butker was able to make multiple field goals in a contest for the first time since Week 6, and most importantly, he didn't miss a kick. The kicker made both field goals in the second quarter, converting attempts from 40 and 44 yards. Butker has now gone 14-for-21 on field-goal tries, including 2-for-8 from 50-plus yards, while converting 31 of 32 PATs over 10 contests so far during the 2026 season.

3055899.headline: Butker made all five PATs in the Chiefs' 35-13 win over the Falcons on Sunday.
3055899.story: Butker did not attempt a field goal in the contest, as the Chiefs solely scored touchdowns. He now moves to 27-for-28 on PATs in 2026 as he continues to struggle to hold onto the starting kicker job.

3055899.headline: Butker will remain Kansas City's kicker ahead of Sunday's game against the Falcons, Sam McDowell of The Kansas City Star reports.
3055899.story: On that topic, coach Andy Reid said Wednesday, "I'm gonna stick with Butker this week." While the veteran kicker has held on to the top job through the Chiefs' first eight games, he's had accuracy issues this season, having converted 12 of his 19 field-goal attempts and making 22 of his 23 extra-point tries in that span. Reid's comment about Butker on Wednesday implies that the team's kicking situation is being evaluated on a weekly basis. Justin Tucker is on Kansas City's practice squad, and he remains an option should Reid decide that a switch is in order down the road.

4432708.headline: Harrison (hamstring) was a full participant in Thursday's practice.
4432708.story: Harrison has missed the Texans' last two contests, but after a limited practice Wednesday, the wideout's full participation Thursday sets the stage for him to return to action Sunday against the Ravens. Given Harrison's modest production over three outings since arriving in a trade with the Cardinals, he profiles as a speculative fantasy lineup option in Week 12, with Nico Collins, Xavier Hutchinson, Tank Dell and possibly Kayshon Boutte (hip, 'DNP' Thursday) also in Houston's WR mix.

4432708.headline: Harrison (hamstring) was listed as a limited participant in Wednesday's practice.
4432708.story: Harrison has been sidelined for the Texans' last two contests, but the WR's ability to practice Wednesday, albeit in a limited fashion, bodes well for his chances of being available for Sunday's game against the Ravens. Harrison's fantasy impact in three outings with Houston since coming over in a trade with Arizona has been modest, so we'd like to see the No. 4 overall pick in the 2024 NFL draft get a full and productive game in before endorsing him as a fantasy lineup option.

4432708.headline: Harrison (hamstring) was at practice Wednesday, Jonathan M. Alexander of the Houston Chronicle  reports.
4432708.story: Harrison has missed two straight games, but his looming practice participation, in any capacity, is a good sign regarding his availability as Sunday's game against the Ravens approaches. The Texans' upcoming injury report will reveal the wideout's official participation level in Wednesday's session.

4432708.headline: Harrison (hamstring) has been ruled out for Thursday night's game against the Colts.
4432708.story: Harrison was also inactive for this past Sunday's game against the Browns, and he will now target a potential return to action Nov. 29 versus the Ravens following Houston's Week 11 bye. In his continued absence, Nico Collins, Xavier Hutchinson, Kayshon Boutte and Tank Dell will handle the Texans' WR duties Thursday. Collins (16 targets, nine catches) and Hutchinson (nine targets, four catches) combined for 152 receiving yards on the 25 targets the duo saw against Cleveland in Week 10.

4432710.headline: Henderson (illness) was placed on injured reserve Saturday, Mike Reiss of ESPN.com reports.
4432710.story: Henderson was already ruled out for Sunday's game against the Lions in Munich, and now that he's on IR, the second-year running back will be required to miss at least the next four games. Henderson's next opportunity to play is Week 15 against the Chiefs on Monday, Dec. 21, although there's no timetable for his return, as he is recovering from "an unexpected and unusual medical emergency involving a series of neurological symptoms." If Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) cannot play Sunday, then the Patriots' backfield will be led by Corey Kiner and Lan Larison.

4432710.headline: Coach Mike Vrabel said Friday that Henderson (illness) is working hard to get back, while acknowledging that he doesn't have a timetable for when that may occur, Mark Daniels of MassLive.com reports.
4432710.story: On the topic of when the running back might return, Vrabel noted Friday, "when that is, I don't know. I don't have a timetable." Henderson, who last saw game action in Week 7, has already been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Lions, and based on Vrabel's statement, the 2025 second-rounder's status beyond the Patriots' Week 11 bye is unclear. Fellow RB Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) returned to a limited practice Thursday, but if he ends up being held out this weekend, Corey Kiner, followed by Lan Larison, would be next up for the team's backfield work versus Detroit, with Terrell Jennings r

4432710.headline: Henderson (illness) didn't practice Wednesday and is listed as out for Sunday's game against the Lions in Munich.
4432710.story: Henderson was one of three players listed as out for this weekend's contest, signaling that they are not in line to make the trip to Germany. With Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) not practicing Wednesday and reportedly on track to miss some time, it looks like Corey Kiner is trending toward leading New England's Week 10 backfield, with Lan Larison also in the mix and Terrell Jennings a potential practice-squad elevation. New England has a bye in Week 11, so Nov. 29 against the Chargers is Henderson's soonest possible return date.

4432710.headline: Henderson (illness) was absent from Wednesday's practice, Evan Lazar of the Patriots' official site reports.
4432710.story: With Henderson and Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) both absent, Corey Kiner and Lan Larison are left as New England's top running backs ahead of a Week 10 matchup in Munich against the Lions on Sunday. After that, the Patriots have a Week 11 bye, and it's still unclear when Henderson might be available again.

5083754.headline: Flournoy wasn't targeted in Thursday's 39-38 loss to the Eagles.
5083754.story: The wideout played 55 off 77 offensive snaps and ran 29 routes on Dak Prescott's 33 dropbacks, but Flournoy was just out there doing cardio against Philadelphia. He has just one catch for 11 yards on one target over the last two games, as CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens are dominating the pass-game looks in Dallas' offense.

5083754.headline: Flournoy caught just one pass for 11 yards on one target in Sunday's 51-30 win over the Titans.
5083754.story: The Cowboys' slot receiver drew just one look on Dak Prescott's 33 pass attempts. He'd caught multiple passes in all 10 games leading up to Sunday's contest. A favorite target of Prescott in the red zone, Flournoy will try to rebound at home against the Eagles on Thanksgiving, when he'll be playable on three-game fantasy slates for Thursday.

5083754.headline: Judging overreactions to NFL Week 11: Joe Brady's Bills impact, Eagles' chances
5083754.story: After watching the Thursday night game, I was all set to do a "Colts need to cut Daniel Jones" item for the Week 11 overreactions column, but Indianapolis went ahead and beat me to it. I'm not sure it would have been an overreaction by me, and I'm not su

4360078.headline: When addressing the press Wednesday, Pierce (heel) noted that the offseason procedure he underwent this past March was done because he was dealing with heel pain that impacted his Achilles, Kevin Bowen of 107.5 The Fan Indianapolis reports.
4360078.story: Additionally, Pierce acknowledged that playing in Week 1 was a bit lofty, per Bowen, with the WR saying Wednesday that he was still managing some pain at that stage. In any case, Pierce indicated that he's confident that his current recovery plan will lead to a full return to health. When that will be remains to be seen, but the 2022 second-rounder is still on IR ahead of Week 12, with the Colts presumably not planning to rush him back given the team's 3-8 record in a campaign that's been marked by the team moving several key players ahead of the trade deadline.

4360078.headline: Head coach Shane Steichen said Monday that Pierce continues to rehab his left heel injury, and the wideout hasn't been ruled out for a return from injured reserve before the end of the season, Nathan Brown of The Indianapolis Star reports.
4360078.story: Steichen rebuffed a report Sunday from Ian Rapoport of NFL Network, who relayed that the Colts were planning to "exercise great caution" by holding Pierce out for the season as he works his way back from an aggravation of his surgically repaired heel. However, given the 3-8 Colts' place in the standings in addition to their $114 million investment in Pierce, Steichen acknowledged that the 26-year-old wideout still faces an uphill battle to make it back from IR before season's end if he's anything less than 100 percent. According to James Boyd of The Athletic, Steichen said that Pierce currentl

4360078.headline: Pierce's season "is almost certainly over" due to the heel injury that landed the wideout on IR on Sept. 26, according to Ian Rapoport of NFL Network.
4360078.story: The 3-8 Colts traded both Josh Downs and Keenan Allen ahead of the NFL trade deadline, and now it appears they'll err on the side of caution with Pierce for the remainder of what has turned into a lost season for the team. With that in mind, Pierce will be able to turn his focus toward returning to full health in advance of the 2027 NFL campaign. Heading into next Sunday's game against the Giants, the Colts will proceed with a WR corps comprised of Laquon Treadwell, Deion Burks, Anthony Gould, Ashton Dulin, Nick Westbrook-Ikhine and Quez Watkins.

4360078.headline: When asked Wednesday whether Pierce (heel) has a chance to return from IR this season, Colts head coach Shane Steichen was noncommittal, James Boyd of The Athletic reports.
4360078.story: "We'll see. Like I said last week, he's still in that rehab process, and I'm not going to put a timetable on return," Steichen noted of the wideout, who's been on IR since Sept. 26. At 2-7, the Colts were sellers ahead of the NFL's trade deadline, so the team presumably has no reason rush Pierce back. With Keenan Allen and Josh Downs no longer in the mix, Indy's healthy WRs for now are Ashton Dulin, Laquon Treadwell, Anthony Gould, Deion Burks and Nick Westbrook-Ikhine.

4685261.headline: Bernard caught one of two targets for 58 yards during the Steelers' 27-5 win over the Broncos on Friday.
4685261.story: Friday was the Steelers' first game with Mason Rudolph under center following a tumultuous few days which saw the team waive veteran quarterback Aaron Rodgers on Wednesday. Rudolph threw for only 142 yards on nine of 15 pass attempts, and a big chunk of that came on Bernard's lone reception of the game in the first quarter, when the second-round rookie caught the ball at the Steelers' 20-yard line and scampered into Broncos territory for a 58-yard catch. Pittsburgh's defense did much of the heavy lifting Friday, but the offense will have more time to game plan with Rudolph at the helm ahead of

4685261.headline: Bernard caught six passes for 40 yards on 10 targets in Sunday's 19-16 loss to the Eagles.
4685261.story: With Michael Pittman (foot) remaining sidelined for Week 11, Bernard retained his every-down role on offense, playing 67 of 71 offensive snaps while leading the team in routes (52) and targets. It was a nice bounce-back game for the rookie after he was held without a catch on three targets against the Bengals in Week 10. Pittman is expected back for Friday's game against the Broncos, but Bernard could keep pacing the team in playing time, especially if DK Metcalf gets disciplined for his latest on-field outburst.

4685261.headline: Bernard failed to reel in any of his three targets while notching a 10-yard rush during Sunday night's 38-18 loss to the Bengals.
4685261.story: Bernard went without a catch for the first time since Week 1, and his three targets were his fewest since the team's Week 4 loss to the Browns. The wide receiver led his position in offensive snaps (58), besting DK Metcalf (50) in that regard. Bernard entered Week 10 having recorded multiple receptions in five straight contests, and he'll have a good shot to get back on track in Week 11 versus the Eagles.

4685261.headline: Bernard caught all five of his targets for 30 yards during Sunday's 27-6 win against Cleveland.
4685261.story: Bernard led the team in catches, reeling in multiple passes for the fifth straight week and sixth time overall this year. The wide receiver has built a strong rapport with starting quarterback Aaron Rodgers, but it's unclear what Bernard's workload will look like after the Steelers have a chance to regroup and potentially acquire another pass catcher during the team's bye week in Week 9.

4361432.headline: Doubs (shoulder), who remains on injured reserve, has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Chargers.
4361432.story: Since the Patriots designated Doubs for return from injured reserve Wednesday, he logged limited listings on injury reports. However, head coach Mike Vrabel told Evan Lazar of the team's official site Friday that Doubs is unlikely to play in Week 12, which now has been confirmed. Doubs will turn his sights to a Week 13 matchup with the Bills on Sunday, Dec. 6.

4361432.headline: Head coach Mike Vrabel said Friday that Doubs (shoulder) likely won't play in Sunday's game against the Chargers, Evan Lazar of the Patriots' official site reports.
4361432.story: Doubs was designated to return from injured reserve earlier in the week, but Vrabel's comments suggest the wide receiver isn't on track to be activated ahead of Sunday's contest. If Doubs remains sidelined, Sunday would mark his fifth consecutive absence. QB Drake Maye (lower leg) and WR A.J. Brown (hamstring) have both been officially ruled out while Doubs' inactive status has yet to be confirmed.

4361432.headline: Doubs (shoulder) was listed as a limited practice participant on Thursday's estimated report.
4361432.story: The Patriots didn't hold a practice on Thanksgiving Day, but Doubs has opened Week 12 prep listed as a limited participant in back-to-back sessions. The fifth-year wide receiver was designated to return from injured reserve Wednesday, and he would need to be activated from IR in order to be available for Sunday's road game against the Chargers. Doubs' return would bolster a Patriots' wide receiver group that will likely be without A.J. Brown (hamstring) for Week 12.

4361432.headline: Doubs (shoulder) was limited in Wednesday's practice.
4361432.story: According to Mike Reiss of ESPN.com, Doubs did individual drills and ran routes against air, suggesting the wide receiver was especially limited after having his 21-day practice window opened earlier in the day. Doubs looks genuinely questionable for Sunday's game against the Chargers.

4686422.headline: Hutchinson caught two of three targets for 13 yards in Thursday night's 26-3 win over the Colts.
4686422.story: Hutchinson played 54 of 66 offensive snaps, second at wide receiver on the team behind Nico Collins' 59, and the former has been operating as the Texans' WR2 in terms of playing time for the last several weeks. By not scoring a touchdown Thursday night, Hutchinson snapped his personal three-game touchdown streak. For the season, he has 30 catches for 358 yards and three scores on 57 targets. He's on pace to set new career highs across the board.

4686422.headline: Hutchinson is expected to continue to benefit from elevated playing time Thursday against the Colts while Marvin Harrison (hamstring) is sidelined for a second straight game, Jared Koch of SI.com reports.
4686422.story: Harrison hasn't exceeded a 50 percent snap share in any of his three appearances with the Texans since coming over in a trade with the Cardinals, but his absence for the Week 10 loss to the Browns still proved beneficial for Hutchinson. The fourth-year wideout out of Iowa State tied his season high with nine targets against the Browns, finishing with four catches for 58 yards and a touchdown while playing more than three-fourths of the offensive snaps for a second consecutive contest. Another healthy snap share should await Hutchinson in Week 11, and he could represent the No. 2 option in the

4686422.headline: Fantasy football free agent pickups: Replacing Drake Maye? Trust in Tyson?
4686422.story: The New England Patriots are one of six teams that will not be playing in Week 11, as bye weeks continue. However, even when the defending AFC champions resume playing in Week 12 versus the Los Angeles Chargers, QB

4686422.headline: Hutchinson brought in four of nine targets for 58 yards and a touchdown in the Texans' 27-24 loss to the Browns on Sunday.
4686422.story: Hutchinson, who was checked for a concussion during the fourth quarter, finished second across the board in receptions, receiving yards and targets for the Texans. He also recorded a touchdown grab for the third straight game on an 11-yard catch early in the second quarter, and his receiving yardage tally was his highest since Week 5. Hutchinson now sports a 28-345-3 receiving line on 54 targets as he continues to function in a steady complementary role heading into a Week 11 home matchup against the Colts on Thursday night.

5082424.headline: Zvada made three of four field-goal attempts and both PATs in Sunday's 23-18 win over the Jaguars.
5082424.story: The rookie kicker continues to have his ups and downs. While he was good from 53, 54 and 43 yards, Zvada missed a chip shot from 32 yards on the opening drive of the second half that left coach John Harbaugh shaking his head. Zvada continues to be a bit of a liability, as he's made just 11 of 18 field-goal attempts over his last six games. Harbaugh is clearly growing more frustrated by the week, and it could lead to the Giants making a move at the position.

5082424.headline: Zvada missed his only field-goal try and made all three of his PATs on Thursday in a loss to Washington.
5082424.story: Zvada's miss was a chip-shot 33-yarder in the first quarter that sailed wide left. That proved to be a critical mistake, as the Commanders won by just three points. Zvada appeared to shore up his job security a bit by going 4-for-4 on FG tries in Week 9 against Philadelphia, but it's hard to ignore the fact that he's gone just 17-for-23 on field-goal attempts overall and has missed three kicks from under 50 yards. The rookie does have a perfect 16-for-16 mark on extra-point attempts, and head coach John Harbaugh expressed support for the inconsistent kicker Friday, saying of Zvada, "I'm confid

5082424.headline: Zvada made all four of his field-goal attempts and his lone PAT in Sunday's 19-11 win over the Eagles.
5082424.story: After Zvada missed both of his field-goal tries in the Giants' pre-Week 8 bye overtime win over the Texans two weeks ago, coach John Harbaugh stuck with the rookie kicker, and Zvada answered with a perfect afternoon against Philly. Zvada accounted for 13 of the team's 19 points, converting field goals from 53, 49, 38 and 49 yards. On the season, he's 17-for-22 on field-goal tries and 13-for-13 on PATs.

5082424.headline: Head coach John Harbaugh reiterated Monday that he's confident in Zvada and said that the Giants have no plans to work out other kickers, Pat Leonard of the New York Daily News reports.
5082424.story: Though the Giants escaped with a 27-21 overtime win over the Texans on Sunday, Zvada had his second rough performance in the past three weeks. The undrafted rookie out of Michigan was unable to connect on field-goal tries of 44 and 56 yards, giving him five misses on 18 attempts through seven games. The Giants are hoping that their upcoming Week 8 bye will give Zvada some time to iron out kinks and refine his approach before the team returns to action Nov. 8 versus the Eagles.

4837248.headline: Fantasy football free agent pickups: Grab your Rams and Packers quickly
4837248.story:
The first thing fantasy managers should know about Week 12 is that the Green Bay Packers and Los Angeles Rams get the week started this Wednesday night.

4837248.headline: Mendoza was 18-for-37 passing for 267 yards, three touchdowns and one interception and had four carries for 22 yards during Sunday's 38-24 loss in Denver.

4837248.story: The Mendoza era in Las Vegas officially kicked off this week following the trade of veteran QB Kirk Cousins to the Vikings, and the rookie first overall pick unsurprisingly flashed at times while also stalling numerous drives by taking six sacks overall. 15864.story: Smith didn't have a completion longer than 21 yards but kept the offense on schedule with an accurate performance. Most importantly, he stepped up in the red zone, which has been the team's Achilles' heel throughout the season. 15864.story: Smith dealt with an ankle injury during the week after he was forced from last Sunday's loss against the Bills, but all scans came back clean, and the veteran quarterback is good to go for a road date in Los Angeles. Smith has been able to get the ball to his playmakers this season, but he doesn't have any fantasy upside as a statuesque pocket passer in an offense that likes to run the ball.

15864.headline: Smith (ankle) will practice Friday, and head coach Aaron Glenn said "things look promising for him playing Sunday," Brian Costello of the New York Post reports.
15864.story: While the initial report indicated only that Smith would practice, Eric Allen of the Jets' official website reported that Smith will be a full participant Friday, which makes it even more likely that he will be under center in Week 11. The Jets' final injury report will reveal whether or not Smith carries an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Chargers.

15864.headline: Smith (ankle) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice.
15864.story: Smith also was deemed limited on Wednesday's practice estimate, so he may need to work fully Friday in order to approach Sunday's game against the Chargers without an injury designation. For his part, the Jets' QB1 isn't worried about his Week 11 availability, with Rich Cimini of ESPN.com noting Wednesday that while Smith still was walking with a noticeable limp at that point, the signal-caller stated that he intends to play this weekend. "That's the plan," Smith said. "Obviously, you've got to take it day by day, but that's the plan."

The 26-year-old QB connected with DeVonta Smith for TDs of 50 yards in the second quarter and 45 yards in the third, before a big fourth quarter in which Milton ran in a 15-yard score of his own and then found Makai Lemon for a 15-yard strike as Philly erased a 38-24 deficit. 4360698.story: Milton has thrown for just 310 yards without a touchdown pass or interception through two starts. He rushed for just seven yards Sunday after notching 64 rushing yards against the Giants in his first start with the Eagles, but Milton avoided mistakes as the Eagles rode their defense and Saquon Barkley's legs to their third win of the season. Twelve of Milton's 21 passes were directed to DeVonta Smith (hamstring) in their first game together. 4360698.story: While starting in his team debut Week 9 against the Giants, Milton was unable to bring an end to the Eagles' lengthy losing streak, but the third-year quarterback showed enough positives to retain the starting gig coming out of a Week 10 bye. Milton put an intriguing dual-threat skill set on display with 64 yards on nine carries to go with 169 passing yards on 34 attempts in the 19-11 loss to New York, with the rushing output in particular perhaps making him worth a look in superflex leagues or leagues that start two quarterbacks. 4241464.headline: Head coach Kyle Shanahan announced that Jones will start in place of Brock Purdy (ankle) on Sunday against the Seahawks.
4241464.story: Purdy didn't practice this week and was ruled out for Week 12 on Friday, setting Jones up for his first start of the campaign. In eight starts for an injured Purdy in 2025, Jones went 5-3, completed 201 of 289 passes (69.6 percent) for 2,151 yards, 13 touchdowns and six interceptions, rushed 28 times for 64 yards and fumbled four times (two lost).

4241464.headline: Jones (illness) is active for Sunday night's matchup against Minnesota, Brooke Evans of the 49ers' official website reports.
4241464.story: Jones is good to go for Sunday Night Football after dealing with an illness at practice throughout the week. The quarterback will operate in his primary reserve role behind starter Brock Purdy versus the Vikings in Mexico City.

4241464.story: Jones popped up on the 49ers' injury report with an unspecified illness Wednesday, and now his status for Week 11 is up in the air. If he can't practice in full Friday, there's a decent chance he'll end up carrying an injury designation into the weekend.

3052587.story: Mayfield fought through foot and thumb injuries to take the field in a critical game for the 3-6 Buccaneers, but he wasn't able to keep pace with Jared Goff and Jahmyr Gibbs. Mayfield did throw multiple touchdown passes for the first time this season, hitting rookie Ted Hurst for scoring strikes of 23 and four yards. 3116407.headline: Rudolph will start Friday's game against the Broncos, Tom Pelissero of The Ringer and Netflix reports.

The Steelers will see if Rudolph can provide a spark for 6-4 Pittsburgh. Rudolph has made 19 career regular-season starts and has averaged 6.6 yards per attempt with a 30:22 TD:INT on 742 pass attempts.

4240391.story: With Drake Maye (fibula) hurt early in Week 10 against Detroit, DeVito stepped in at quarterback but managed to complete just 12 of 24 pass attempts for 81 yards, a touchdown and an interception. He added 19 yards on four carries. The 28-year-old does have some starting experience -- he helmed the Giants offense for eight starts between 2023 and 2024 -- but he didn't play at all in 2025. For now, the Patriots are at least communicating that they'll stand pat and not look for help at quarterback outside the organization. However, the team is barely hanging on in the AFC playoff race with a 5-5

4240391.headline: Head coach Mike Vrabel said Friday that DeVito will start in Week 12 against the Chargers on Nov. 29, Mike Reiss and Adam Schefter of ESPN.com report.
4240391.story: Drake Maye was diagnosed with a fractured right fibula, which he sustained in the first quarter of the Patriots' 35-10 loss to the Lions in Week 10 in Munich. DeVito filled in for the rest of that contest and completed 12 of 24 passes for 81 yards, one touchdown and one interception while turning four carries into 19 yards. DeVito looks like he'll be New England's starter coming out of the bye, with rookie seventh-round pick Behren Morton operating as the backup.

4240391.story: Regarding Maye's status going forward, head coach Mike Vrabel indicated that he'll wait for further information before estimating how long his starting QB might be out, but he also acknowledged he "wouldn't imagine him being available coming out of the (Week 11) bye," Phil Perry of NBC Sports Boston reports. As a result, DeVito is in a position to start Sunday, Nov. 29 against the Chargers and possibly beyond. 4240391.story: Drake Maye (ankle) was forced to leave the game early after an Aidan Hutchinson (knee) sack, putting DeVito under center for the third time this season, but the first time with the outcome still in doubt. The 28-year-old QB had little luck moving the ball, and his 10-yard TD toss to Lan Larison in the fourth quarter came when the score was already 28-3. The severity of Maye's ankle injury isn't yet known, but the Patriots fortunately get a bye in Week 11 to give him extra recovery time. If he's still unavailable after that, DeVito could find himself starting in Week 12 against the Chargers.

A 2023 first-round pick, Richardson himself hasn't started since Week 16 of the 2024 campaign, making just four brief appearances the past two seasons combined, but he'll have a chance to boost his value (or not) in the final year of his rookie contract.

4429020.headline: Uiagalelei (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the emergency third quarterback against the Bills on Sunday, Eric Smith of the Chargers' official site reports.

11394.headline: Head coach Mike LaFleur said Wednesday that Johnson is preparing to start Sunday's game versus the Commanders due to Carson Beck's back injury, Dani Sureck of the Cardinals' official site reports.
11394.story: Beck won't practice Wednesday due to continued issues with back spasms, which held him out of this past Sunday's loss in Kansas City. In place of Beck, Johnson completed 18 of 31 passes for 155 yards and one touchdown while also taking two carries for five yards. Friday's injury report will reveal if Beck has a chance to play in Week 12, and by proxy if Johnson will get another spot start.

11394.story: The 40-year-old QB was pressed into duty with rookie Carson Beck (back) on the shelf, and Johnson unsurprisingly wasn't really up to the task after the Cardinals fell into a 14-0 hole before the first quarter was over. Johnson spent most of his afternoon finding Trey McBride for short gains, and he did hit Simi Fehoko for a two-yard score in the second quarter. Beck doesn't figure to miss much time, but if Johnson gets another start in Week 12, he'll be taking on a much less formidable Commanders defense.

When asked if Darnold is 100 percent, head coach Mike Macdonald told Bell that "pretty much nobody is fully health at this point in the season," indicating that the quarterback still may be dealing with residual effects of those health concerns. In any case, Darnold will resume starting duties for the Seahawks this weekend.

3912547.headline: Darnold (quadriceps) practiced fully Wednesday, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
3912547.story: Head coach Mike Macdonald told Brady Henderson of ESPN.com on Wednesday that Darnold will start Sunday at San Francisco if he fares well in practice this week, and a full practice is a good place for the quarterback to kick things off. Darnold has missed the last two contests due to a quad injury and cracked ribs, but only the first concern was mentioned on Wednesday's practice report, indicating his improved level of health.

3912547.story: Darnold missed the Seahawks' last two games while tending to a pair of injuries, but he appears to be feeling healthier coming out of a Week 11 bye. While Macdonald stopped just short of confirming him the team's Week 12 starter, Darnold should get the nod if he's able to practice without restrictions Wednesday and occurs no setbacks along the way.

4879194.story: Despite being on the field for only 25 of the Jaguars' 68 offensive snaps in Week 11, Cameron drew a career-high seven targets. 4879194.story: Cameron gave the Jaguars a 14-point lead early in the fourth quarter when he hauled in a 25-yard touchdown pass from Trevor Lawrence. It was the rookie wideout's third touchdown of the campaign but his first since Week 3. Cameron's 67 receiving yards marked a career high, while his three receptions tied the most he's had as a pro. Cameron's propensity for finding the end zone (his three TDs have come on just 12 total catches) is appealing, but at this point he isn't getting enough volume to be a reliable week-to-week fantasy asset.
